claims.text: Henry Moore Grants support the growth and development of sculpture across historical, modern and contemporary registers.
Henry Moore Grants fund research that expands the appreciation of sculpture.
Applications are considered four times per year.
The deadline for the Autumn round is September 1st at 23:00.
Projects funded in the Autumn round must start or open to the public no sooner than January 1st, 2027.
Applications for the Winter round open on November 1st at 9:00.
The deadline for the Winter round is December 1st at 23:00.
Projects funded in the Winter round must start or open to the public no sooner than April 1st, 2027.
Applications for the Spring round open on February 1st, 2027 at 9:00.
The deadline for the Spring round is March 1st, 2027 at 23:00.
Projects funded in the Spring round must start or open to the public no sooner than July 1st, 2027.
Applications for the Summer round open on May 1st, 2027 at 9:00.
The deadline for the Summer round is June 1st, 2027 at 23:00.
Projects funded in the Summer round must start or open to the public no sooner than October 1st, 2027.
Registration requests must be received one week before the deadline.
The maximum grant available for New Projects and Commissions is £20,000.
The maximum grant available for Acquisitions and Collections is £20,000.
The maximum grant available for Conferences, Lectures and Publications is £5,000.
The maximum grant available for Long-Term Research grants is £20,000.
The maximum grant available for Research and Travel grants is £2,500.

Henry Moore Grants are available to UK and international non-profit organisations for exhibitions, exhibition catalogues, commissions, conferences, research, non-commercial publications and the development of collections.
Individual sculpture historians, academics and conservators can apply to the Research and Travel category.
Individuals are not accepted if they are independently wishing to create, inform, develop or research their own practice.
Community project applications will only be considered when the applicant is a non-profit arts organisation.
The Artist Award Scheme is not a grant that can be applied for.
